Paleontologists often only have morphological data, measured from fossil
specimens, to work with when doing phylogenetic reconstruction. In this lab,
we will explore some basic approaches to morphological phylogenetics, including
character mapping, dealing with sparse / missing data, and parsimony 
reconstruction from fossil characters. 

Let's say you happen upon your biologist friend's field journal, which
contains fossil descriptions for five previously unknown lizard species. 
These descriptions can be found in the file `lizard_descriptions.txt` in your
assignment folder.  From these descriptions, construct 2-3 characters that can 
be mapped to each  species for downstream analysis. You can decide which 
characters are important, and whether to encode them as discrete qualitative 
states, integer counts, continuous measurements, etc. Note that data may be
missing for some combinations of species / characters; this is often the case
for fossil records and you can decide how to encode missing observations. 
Note that for morphological characters, it is important to distinguish between
features that are *observed to be absent* from a complete skeleton and those
that are *missing* because of a lack of preservation.

In the phylogenetics package `phangorn`, the function `bab()`, builds a phylogeny
from a character matrix using the parsimony *branch and bound* method, which we
discussed in class. Parsimony methods are still commonly used in morphological 
phylogenetics due to difficulties in constructing distance corrections for 
morphological characters, and because synapomorphies that can be used for 
taxonomic classification naturally fall out of parsimony analyses. 

Using your constructed character matrix, infer the most parsimonious tree(s)
using `phangorn::bab()`. Note that, depending on your character matrix
, you may have to convert continuous characters into discrete ones. For example, 
you could convert a body size measurement into "small" and "large" using a 
threshold value. 

```{r}
```
